question: us-policy-positions:environment-energy.price-carbon
definition: yes = on 1/1/2026 the state was participating in a binding carbon-pricing program with allowances sold or traded at a market price: a RGGI CO2 Budget Trading Program (power sector only), California cap-and-trade/cap-and-invest (economy-wide) or Washington's Climate Commitment Act cap-and-invest (economy-wide). no = no such program in force on that date, including Virginia (withdrawn 2024-2025, resumes 7/1/2026), Pennsylvania (rule struck, withdrew 11/2025), New York's unlaunched cap-and-invest and Oregon's Climate Protection Program (declining cap with free instruments, no auction). States outside those programs are no by elimination from the complete list of U.S. carbon-pricing programs (marked weak).
summarySource: rggi.org Elements of RGGI and state regulations pages (fetched 9/28/2026, 2026 cap for eleven states), RGGI 'Welcome Virginia' statement 4/29/2026, CARB Cap-and-Invest program page (2026), RCW 70A.65 (app.leg.wa.gov), Oregon DEQ CPP page, Wikipedia RGGI and Climate Commitment Act articles.
